prompt.context: Your client is OrthoGel, a medical device company that manufactures a hydrogel used in surgeries to help patients recover. The gel is applied with a biodegradable sponge. OrthoGel is considering a deal with a sponge manufacturer, SpongeBob, to combine the gel with a sponge to create a hybrid product. SpongeBob would be in charge of the sales & marketing of the final product.
prompt.question: Should OrthoGel make a deal with SpongeBob? If so, what should OrthoGel negotiate?

clarifying_info.q: What is the proposed deal structure?
clarifying_info.a: OrthoGel would sell directly to SpongeBob, who would then handle sales & marketing of the final combined product.
The financial target is to maintain or improve profitability.

clarifying_info.q: What does the combined product offer customers?
clarifying_info.a: The combined product allows for greater efficiency in post-op recovery.
Market size is large — not a relevant constraint for this analysis.
OrthoGel is the market leader and has unique IP. Sponges are a commodity with multiple vendors.

clarifying_info.q: How many sponges are needed per vial?
clarifying_info.a: A clinic needs 3 sponges per vial. Products are single-use.

clarifying_info.q: What is the willingness to pay for each product?
clarifying_info.a: WTP for the gel vial is $50; WTP for a sponge is $10.

clarifying_info.q: How does the combined product affect WTP?
clarifying_info.a: WTP increases by 15% for the combined product.

clarifying_info.q: What does it cost SpongeBob to manufacture a sponge?
clarifying_info.a: It costs SpongeBob $2 to manufacture a sponge.

exhibits.title: Price Potential (Verbal)
exhibits.shows: Pricing information provided verbally by the interviewer, covering willingness-to-pay for the gel vial, sponge, and combined product, as well as usage ratios.
exhibits.data: WTP vial=$50; WTP sponge=$10; WTP combined product = +15% premium; clinic uses 3 sponges per vial; products are single-use; sponges are a commodity

exhibits.title: OrthoGel Financial Analysis
exhibits.shows: A cost breakdown table comparing OrthoGel's per-unit COGS in the stand-alone scenario vs. the combined product scenario, across Materials, Manufacturing, Packaging, Labor, and Sales & Marketing line items. Revenue price is shown for stand-alone only. SpongeBob's sponge manufacturing cost is noted separately.
exhibits.data: Stand-Alone: Price/unit=$50; Materials=$1.00; Manufacturing=$0.25; Packaging=$0.15; Labor=$2.10; Sales & Marketing=$1.50 | Combined: Materials=$0.90; Manufacturing=$0.20; Packaging=$0.10; Labor=$1.80; Sales & Marketing=$0.50 | SpongeBob sponge cost=$2/sponge

framework: Deal structure: Evaluate whether to do the deal (Yes/No) and what terms to negotiate if yes — up-front payment, royalty, revenue-sharing, greater upsell
If Yes: Negotiate price OrthoGel charges SpongeBob, royalty structure, and value capture given OrthoGel drives the bulk of WTP
If No: Explore alternatives — build sponges in-house, find a different partner, maintain direct sales channel
Market: Assess market size, customer WTP, competitive alternatives, insurance reimbursement, and regulatory hurdles
Company capabilities: Manufacturing feasibility, selling capacity, marketing strength

questions.prompt: Calculate the current combined price to the customer and the new WTP for the combined product — first with 1 sponge, then with 3 sponges per vial.
questions.guidance: Candidate should use WTP figures to compute current price and then apply the 15% WTP uplift for the hybrid product. Strong candidates will note the relative value contributions of each party.

math.setup: WTP vial=$50, WTP sponge=$10, combined WTP premium=15%. With 1 sponge: current price=$50+$10=$60; with 3 sponges: current price=$50+(3x$10)=$80.
math.answer: 1-sponge: current $60, combined WTP $69. 3-sponge: current $80, combined WTP $92. OrthoGel contributes 83% of value in the 1-sponge case and 62.5% in the 3-sponge case.

questions.prompt: Using Exhibit 2, calculate OrthoGel's total COGS in the stand-alone and combined scenarios. What price should OrthoGel charge SpongeBob to maintain its current unit margin?
questions.guidance: Candidate should sum the COGS lines for each scenario, then use the current stand-alone unit margin (revenue minus total cost) as the target margin to determine the minimum transfer price.

steps: SpongeBob revenue from customer (1 sponge, WTP $69): $69 - $48.50 - $2.00 = $18.50 margin
SpongeBob revenue from customer (3 sponge, WTP $92): $92 - $48.50 - $6.00 = $37.50 margin
math.answer: OrthoGel should charge SpongeBob at least $48.50 per vial to maintain its $45 unit margin. SpongeBob's margin drops significantly from ~80% stand-alone to approximately 27-41% depending on sponge bundle. A great candidate notes that the value premium comes primarily from the gel, so OrthoGel has negotiating leverage to charge above $48.50.

brainstorming.prompt: What other financial and non-financial considerations should OrthoGel think about before finalizing the deal?

categories.name: Financial — Revenue
ideas: Charge more given higher WTP (value-based pricing or % margin capture)
Consider cannibalization implications if combined product undercuts stand-alone gel
Negotiate a royalty or revenue-sharing arrangement with SpongeBob
Offer volume-based discounting to incentivize SpongeBob to scale

categories.name: Financial — Costs
ideas: Further minimize COGS with volume-based manufacturing agreements
Reallocate headcount (e.g., reduce Sales & Marketing) if deal goes through

categories.name: Non-Financial — Operations
ideas: Assess manufacturing feasibility of integrating with SpongeBob's process
Evaluate regulatory implications of a new combined device
Understand changes to service and support requirements

categories.name: Non-Financial — Competition
ideas: Assess other sponge manufacturers for a potentially better partnership
Evaluate sales & marketing benefits if deal proceeds — enter new markets or capture new customers

recommendation: The deal creates value for both parties and OrthoGel should proceed, but should negotiate aggressively given that OrthoGel's gel drives the disproportionate share of WTP (62-83% of value depending on sponge count)
OrthoGel should charge SpongeBob at least $48.50 per vial to maintain current unit margins; ideally negotiate a higher transfer price or royalty to capture more of the WTP uplift
SpongeBob's margins drop significantly (from ~80% to ~27-41%), which means SpongeBob has limited room — OrthoGel should also evaluate alternative sponge partners since sponges are a commodity
risks: SpongeBob may reject unfavorable terms and OrthoGel loses combined product benefit
Regulatory approval for the combined device could be lengthy and uncertain
Cannibalization of stand-alone gel sales if combined product is positioned incorrectly
Dependence on a single sponge partner for a core component
next_steps: Conduct due diligence on SpongeBob's manufacturing capabilities and financial health
Engage regulatory counsel to map out approval pathway for the combined device
Model scenarios for transfer price above $48.50 to capture more of the WTP premium
Evaluate at least one alternative sponge manufacturer as leverage in negotiations
